evidence: One named owner: page titles are '<name> | Brand & Product Designer' and every case-study title carries the owner's name (src/App.jsx ROUTES).
Content is a project index (work.projects-list) and four client case studies (/work/*), an about page (/studio) and a personal art practice (/art-lab).
Conversion is a personal enquiry form and a direct e-mail (conversion.lead-form, conversion.studio-cta), not a sign-up, trial or pricing table.
The shop is a small personal art shop of five editions, all sold out (src/lib/shop/products.js soldOut: true on every product); it is a sideline of the portfolio, not a commerce product.

No pricing tiers, accounts, dashboards for visitors, integrations or B2B buyer flows exist on any of the 15 routes. The dashboards inside one case study are recreations of a client's internal tools shown as portfolio work.
classification.decidedBy: agent classification from evidence (pending architecture review)

rules: Generated pages never reproduce the owner's identity, likeness, wordmark, clients, client work, artworks, award badge, URLs or copy (GENERATED_MODE_* in schema/semantic_validate.py).
The award ribbon (shell.awwwards-badge) is optional in every template and forbidden in generated mode (GENERATED_MODE_RATING).
Asset availability is pinned in code (PINNED_AVAILABILITY in the validator and verify_all), not only in assets/asset-roles.json.
Runtime/utility UI is retrievalEligible:false and pinned (RETRIEVAL_INELIGIBLE).
Style overrides are catalog tokens only (tokens/llm/token-policy.json); raw colours, raw lengths and other fonts are rejected.
Case studies are decomposed into header / role / context / process / 3-10 heading-bounded chapters / next-project; legal pages into a header and one clause per heading.

approval.note: Category and binding were chosen by an agent from the evidence above. Only the human owner can ratify them; record who, when and what verbatim here when that happens.
